final.title: When rounding becomes a workflow problem
final.body:
If your business keeps saying “rounding claims” as a vague complaint, it stays hard to automate and easy to argue about. I would turn it into one bounded workflow decision: where do small numerical gaps actually change what you do?

Think of the recurring places where two slightly different numbers show up: invoice rounding, currency conversion, timesheet variance, or an estimate-to-actual mismatch. The point is not the label. The point is whether someone has to decide if the gap matters.

Then draw the control boundary. Which cases are already policy, like rounding to the nearest cent? Which cases need human judgment, like flagging a gap above your threshold? Which cases have no rule yet? If the difference is invisible and acceptable, it can stay in the background. If it is visible and affects approval or audit notes, it needs a clear human step.

The practical next step is simple: write one rule in plain English for one recurring workflow. For example, “round amounts to the nearest cent; flag any gap above my threshold for review before I approve the invoice.” Then ask yourself: do I already document why I accepted the difference, or do I just let it pass? If you cannot write the rule clearly yet, fix the policy first. The machine can wait; paperwork rarely does.
